title: Grateful Dead Live at Universal Amphitheatre on 1973-07-01
lineage: aud> Sony ec M22P mics >Sony 770 MR> R1> DAT> CDR

ai_review.summary: Exceptional early‑70s audience tape with crystal‑clear guitar and a monster Playin’ / Truckin’ / The Other One second set.
ai_review.review: This July‑1‑1973 recording is hailed as one of the best pre‑74 audience tapes, delivering a surprisingly crisp, “modern Neumann” sound that captures the band’s dynamics with vivid clarity. The show shines on the second‑set marathon – Playin’ in the Band, Truckin’, The Other One and Space are repeatedly called out as epic jams, while Loose Lucy and Mississippi Half‑Step add extra sparkle. Although a few reviewers note slightly low vocals or minor skipping in Truckin’, the overall listening experience is energetic, tight, and highly immersive.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 4–5 stars, praising both the musical performance (especially the second‑set jams) and the surprisingly excellent audience recording quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the tape as crisp, clear and “like a modern Neumann onstage mix,” with minimal hiss, good pitch, and only occasional minor skipping in Truckin'. Vocals are noted as slightly low but still audible.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower → Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set delivers a solid folk‑rock mix; the second set launches into an epic jam corridor beginning with Playin' and flowing through Truckin', The Other One, and Space, providing the high‑energy highlight that reviewers repeatedly celebrate.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his aggressive, crisp guitar tone – “prime Garcia,” “sweet sweet geetar,” and dynamic playing especially on Playin' and the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as loud and crisp; one reviewer calls Phil’s bombs on The Other One spectacular, though another suggests a slight boost would help hear Lesh better.
